To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

patients with psoriasis who initially engaged in active coping strategies (i.e. expression of emotions, social support, distraction) had a more favourable outcome on anxiety, depression, and physical health 1 year later.
illness perceptions are related to health outcomes and coping is related to health outcomes in psoriasis.
illness perceptions and coping strategies are important predictors of functional status (physical and mental) in patients with psoriasis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role that patients’ illness perceptions and their coping strategies may play in the course and outcome of psoriasis.
the relationship between patients’ illness perceptions and their coping, and their functional status and psychological distress.
the role of illness perception and coping in the adjustment process of patients with psoriatic disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the illness perception and coping style of patients with psori­ asis are important determinants of their functional status and health‐related quality of life.
the illness perceptions are related to the outcome of the disease, but the coping is related to the outcome and the illness perceptions.
the illness perception of psoriasis and coping style of patients are important predictors of the outcome of the disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the illness perception of patients with psoriases is associated with their functional status.
the illness identity and coping style are important factors that should be taken into account when treating patients with psoriasis.
patients with a strong belief in the illness and in the controllability of the illness are more likely to have a poorer outcome in the long term.
The main takeaway from our work is that

patients with psoriasis who are less anxious, less depressive and have better physical health are more likely to engage in coping that is characterized by more expression and less suppression of emotions, seeking social support and distraction, and less use of denial, and passive coping.
patients’ perceptions and coping styles may be important factors to consider in clinical practice.
illness perception and coping should be considered in the management of psoriasis.
